head.i: Verf. 12. Væ ædificanti urbem in sanguine, & qui compingit civitatem per injustitiam !

main_text.p: §. 1. Opus, quod novus molitur regni Christi adversarius, vocatur עיר urbs et קריה civitas. Non est hæc civitas Dei de quâ diximus ad verf. 8. Sed civitas oppofita, regno Christi contraria, cujus etiam fit mentio Num. 24: 19. Psal. 55: 10. Hof. 11: 9. quæ in apocalypsi vocatur Babylon spiritualis Apoc. 11: 8. 14: 8. 16: 19. 17: 5. Proin[?] hujus civitatis conditor est caput istius urbis, & Christo oppositus, qui in scripturis N. T. Antichristus dicitur, quasi alius Nebucadnezar, Spiritualis Babylonis auctor.

Hoc ædificandæ civitatis molimen non debet accipi de urbis cujusdam materialis exstructione; quasi in ædium structurâ, aut murorum externorum circumvallatione consisteret: verum in regni cœlestis mutatione, quâ civitatem Dei in Rempublicam terrestrem, & regnum mundanum transformare laboraret. page.notes: The outline line marked "ב[?]" is a Hebrew letter that I could not read with certainty. The Hebrew words עיר and קריה are copied as I read them; their vowel points are not clearly visible. "Proin[?]" is partly obscured where the word runs into "hujus". The catchword "rā" is the continuation of "terrâ" printed at the foot of the page. The page has no marginal notes.
